_comment: Permission targets are matched as LITERAL PREFIXES here, not regexes.
Verified empirically: `command(gcloud projects list)` matches
`gcloud projects list --limit=1`, while `command(gcloud .* describe)` matches
nothing at all. Never put `.*` in a rule here - it is read as a literal,
so the rule never fires and nothing reports that it did not.
Because a verb like `describe` comes LAST, a prefix rule cannot express
'any gcloud command ending in describe'. So gcloud and bq are allowed broadly
and the PreToolUse hook does the real work: it force_asks every mutation
(force_ask provably overrides allow) and denies unverified or prohibited ones.
This is safe ONLY while the hook is installed - bootstrap.sh blocks the install
if the gate self-test fails, and --uninstall retracts these grants.
Every command also needs a matching unsandboxed(...) grant; the command()
check passes first and then a separate unsandboxed() check runs.
The two read_file allows cover the harness's own files: skill assets and
templates under the plugin dir, and the startup profile every capability
reads on almost every turn. Without them a founder is asked to approve
reading our own template, which teaches them to click through prompts - the
exact habit the approval gate depends on them not having. Neither path holds
secrets, and the credential deny below outranks both.
read_file deny targets must be ABSOLUTE directory paths with no glob. A `~`
breaks sandbox setup entirely ('non-absolute file path') and a `/**` suffix
matches nothing. $HOME is expanded by bootstrap.sh at install time.
_local_tooling_comment: The git/which/ls/terraform-plan grants exist to protect the approval gate,
not to weaken it. A single Conductor track (§10.5) issued 59 shell steps, 48
of them plain git. Ungranted, a founder clicks approve 59 times to land one
small security fix - and arrives at the gcloud mutation that actually matters
with a well-trained reflex to approve. Prompt fatigue is the one failure the
review guarantee cannot survive, so noise is a safety problem here.
The list is what Conductor was observed to run, not what it might run:
status, log, commit, add, notes, config, diff, show. Every entry is LOCAL.
git push, pull, fetch, clone and remote are deliberately absent - push is the
one git verb that sends a founder's code off their machine, and it should
keep prompting. checkout and branch are absent too: unused, and checkout can
terraform is granted only for plan/validate/fmt. Bare `terraform` is not
granted, and apply/destroy/import are force_asked by OPAQUE_EXEC in the hook
regardless - force_ask overrides allow, so no grant here can expose the cloud.
Founder-facing one-liner if asked: local git is not gated; anything that
touches your cloud or leaves your machine is.
_sandbox_comment: enableTerminalSandbox is left at Antigravity's default of false, on purpose.
Turning it on confines the filesystem to the workspace, and gcloud writes to
~/.config/gcloud on nearly every call - token cache, logs, credentials.db. So
`gcloud auth list` dies with 'Read-only file system' and the founder gets a
'run without sandbox restrictions?' prompt for a harmless read. Training
founders to click through prompts is the one habit the approval gate cannot
survive, so a sandbox that half-works is worse here than none.
The review guarantee never depended on it: that is the PreToolUse hook.
The key is not written at all: false is already the default, and agy strips
default-valued keys on every run, so writing it would churn the file forever.
